title: The ENMO+MAD pair, completed: mean amplitude deviation (a newly-authored op) bit-for-bit against GGIR

dataset.name: PAMAP2 Physical Activity Monitoring Dataset
dataset.record: subject 101 hand accelerometer (x, y, z in g at 100 Hz), ~62 min free-living (749 epochs of 5 s)
dataset.citation: Reiss A, Stricker D. Introducing a new benchmarked dataset for activity monitoring. 2012 16th International Symposium on Wearable Computers, IEEE, 2012:108-109.

proposition: ENMO and MAD are the two workhorse accelerometer movement-intensity metrics. The ecosystem's ENMO (computeENMO) is already certified against GGIR, but it had no MAD (mean amplitude deviation) -- the gravity-robust metric that measures the VARIATION of the acceleration vector magnitude within an epoch rather than its elevation above 1 g. This case introduces a NEWLY-AUTHORED op, computeMAD, completing the pair. On a real free-living hand-accelerometer recording it reproduces GGIR::g.applymetrics MAD to MACHINE PRECISION (max |diff| ~5e-14 g, correlation 1.0) across all 749 five-second epochs; the MAD ranges 5-1222 mg (mean 232 mg) -- a physical movement profile.

claims.statement: max |computeMAD - GGIR g.applymetrics MAD| over all epochs (g) -- bit-exact
correlation between computeMAD and GGIR MAD across epochs
number of 5 s epochs certified against GGIR
mean MAD across the recording (mg) -- a physical movement-intensity descriptor
peak epoch MAD (mg) -- the most vigorous 5 s of movement

validation.reference: The newly-authored computeMAD op is validated against the field-standard GGIR::g.applymetrics MAD on the identical PAMAP2 hand-acc signal (both in g). Both compute the per-epoch mean absolute deviation of the vector magnitude r = sqrt(x^2+y^2+z^2) about its epoch mean; the agreement is MACHINE PRECISION (max |diff| ~5e-14 g, correlation 1.0) across all 749 epochs. On this real free-living recording MAD ranges 5-1222 mg (mean 232 mg).
validation.data: REAL -- PAMAP2 (UCI/PhysioNet), subject 101 hand accelerometer, ~62 min free-living, 749 epochs of 5 s at 100 Hz
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the newly-authored computeMAD reproduces GGIR::g.applymetrics MAD to machine precision (max |diff| ~5e-14 g, correlation 1.0) across all 749 epochs; (2) the recording's MAD ranges 5-1222 mg (mean 232 mg), a physical movement profile. HONEST scope: (1) this op is NEWLY AUTHORED to fill a gap -- the ecosystem had ENMO (computeENMO, GGIR-certified) but not MAD, the complementary gravity-robust movement metric; (2) this is a genuine MACHINE-PRECISION match -- the op and GGIR compute the IDENTICAL per-epoch mean-absolute-deviation of the vector magnitude, so the ~5e-14 residual is the floating-point floor, not a convention agreement; (3) MAD and ENMO are genuinely complementary: MAD measures the VARIATION of the magnitude within an epoch (insensitive to a static orientation offset), whereas ENMO measures its ELEVATION above 1 g -- which is the reason to add it; (4) MAD is a physical quantity (g / mg) on real free-living data, so the mean/max/min are meaningful movement descriptors, not reproducibility placeholders; (5) run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: MAD and ENMO are now both available and GGIR-certified; deriving MAD-based physical-activity intensity cut-points (Vaha-Ypya et al. 2015 give sedentary/light/moderate/vigorous MAD thresholds) and comparing the intensity classification against the ENMO cut-points on the same recording would turn the two metrics into a cross-validated activity-intensity layer. Documented, not escalated.
